findings.desc: Offline pack-boundary proof can false-pass an unsatisfied external dependency range. resolveOfflineDependencyGraph carries request.range from every product/transitive manifest (lines 263-290) but visit never compares that range with the resolved installed manifest.version; it keys solely by name@version. buildOfflineCache then rewrites all dependency edges to file: tarballs (lines 464-475), and the consumer installs with root overrides built from those tarballs (lines 632-668). Thus a coordinated manifest+lock mutation such as zod:^99.0.0 while the workspace still resolves zod 4.4.3 is not rejected by graph resolution and can be forced through npm by the override, so the claimed clean offline closed-graph proof is not fail-closed. Add a semver satisfaction check for every request edge (including product seeds, dependencies, and required peers), bind requested ranges/edge provenance into the cache graph/manifest, and add an inverse self-test that mutates an external range to reject the installed version and proves refusal before cache/install.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed by 5aca69cae5: verifier validates each external dependency, optional dependency, and peer dependency request against resolved name and version before creating file overrides; unsupported specs fail closed. The incompatible ^2.0.0 request to installable 1.0.0 mutation is rejected, and range semantics are cache and transcript bound.

findings.desc: doc-code-drift: docs/requirements/decisions/proof-or-stop-identity-cutover.md:37-45,160-172 promises tracked-token classification and mentions case-insensitive searches, but never states that Unicode-escaped JSON spellings are decoded and classified as retired identity residue. findings.desc: packages/main/src/cli.ts:27-41 and bin/bootstrap-runner.js:158-172 declare lab_create and lab_run as mainSharedMutating but admit both in all active-Story phases. cli-engine.ts:856-869 then bypasses the normal phaseTools gate for those rows, while packages/lab/src/handlers/lab.ts:219-283 writes experiment configs/directories, creates sandboxes, and persists baseline/run artifacts; mainSharedMutating also intentionally avoids the per-Story owner lease. Therefore any session can run material-writing Lab operations during REVIEW/TEST and invalidate a supposedly frozen candidate instead of being forced back to DEV. The new tests exercise nested routing only without an active Story and do not catch this lifecycle escape. Keep read-only lab help/eval/compare/promote available broadly, but constrain mutating create/run to a justified lifecycle phase or make lifecycle/ownership arg-aware for genuinely non-writing dry-run behavior.

findings.desc: packages/main/src/cli-engine.ts:856-869 does not prove that a declared extension command is actually external: isDeclaredExtensionCommand checks only that cmd appears in extraOwnershipClasses and extraAllowedPhases. It does not reject overlap with MAIN_TOOLS/COMMAND_POLICIES or require membership in opts.extraTools/the injected handler set. A bootstrap extension can therefore list an existing core command in both metadata maps and bypass the active-Story phase restriction of that core command; resolveEffectiveOwnershipClass keeps the core ownership policy, but the separate phase gate has already been skipped. This contradicts the adjacent claim that optional extension rows are commands outside the core lifecycle registry and turns an extension metadata typo/collision into a core lifecycle escape. Fail closed on core-name overlap and enforce exact parity among extraTools, registered extension handlers, ownership rows, and lifecycle rows, with an active-Story collision test.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed in cade1bf954: extension admission requires a genuine extraTools member with exact ownership/phase metadata and handler, rejects MAIN_TOOLS collisions, and the E2E mutation harness proves core collisions fail closed.

findings.desc: doc-promise-undelivered: docs/CLI.md:1095-1097 and lab_help now call nested lab create/run/eval/compare/promote/help canonical, but the canonical nested help path loses its spelling after alias normalization. Thus execution routing is real, but the product help surface still teaches the compatibility spelling as primary, contradicting the new canonical-command promise. Preserve a canonical display invocation through help rendering and assert exact nested headings/usages for all six subcommands, while testing flat commands separately as compatibility.

findings.desc: scripts/verify-global-lab-entrypoint.mjs:96-118 runs nested lab create/run/eval only against createTempProject(), whose initialized default branch has no active Story; only lab help at :84-95 happens to run from the B-022e story branch. findings.desc: quality-security: packages/main/src/cli-engine.ts:863 accepts any key present in extraOwnershipClasses + extraAllowedPhases as an extension command without proving the key belongs to extraTools or is disjoint from MAIN_TOOLS. A targeted REVIEW harness showed normal red_evidence_create is rejected by its PLAN-only lifecycle policy, but the same core command supplied in those two maps bypasses the phase gate and reaches argument validation. Independently, lines 1246 and 1389 trust the raw external readOnly row rather than the core-first effective ownership resolver, so the same core-name collision suppresses pre/post hooks and Codex process events even though ownership-gate.ts correctly retains the core mutating policy. This is a fail-closed admission and audit bypass; validate exact extraTools membership, reject core-name collisions, and derive hook/event behavior only from that validated declaration.

findings.desc: quality-security: packages/main/src/cli/extension-admission.ts:75-85 validates only that every admitted external name appears somewhere in the final registry; it neither rejects extra handlers nor proves MAIN_TOOLS handlers retain their original function identity after extraRegister. packages/main/src/registry.ts:160-162 exposes override(), so a targeted harness declared one fully valid external_probe, registered its handler, then called registry.override("story_get", ...); validateExternalCommandHandlers passed and the real core story_get printed OVERRIDDEN_CORE_HANDLER. This contradicts extension-admission.ts:21-24 that MAIN_TOOLS remain core-owned and leaves core lifecycle handlers replaceable behind valid-looking four-table metadata. Capture the core registry before extraRegister and fail if any core handler identity changes or any newly registered handler lies outside the admitted external set; add an executable override mutation.

The committed mutation harness overrides story_get with an evil handler and proves admission fails closed while canonical story_get remains unchanged; fresh 120-command validate passed.

findings.desc: concept-cleanup: packages/main/src/cli/extension-admission.ts:75-85 only proves that each admitted external command has some registered handler; it does not prove the registered handler set is exact or that core handlers remain core-owned after extraRegister. Independent executable reproduction on cade1bf954 registered one valid external_probe, then registry.override("story_get", evil); validateExternalCommandHandlers still returned PASS and registry.get("story_get") returned OVERRIDDEN_CORE_HANDLER. This directly violates extension-admission.ts:21-24 and leaves the F-038 resolution incomplete: an extension with otherwise valid extraTools/ownership/phase rows can replace a lifecycle-gated core handler or register undeclared handlers. Snapshot core handler identities before extraRegister, reject any changed core handler and any newly registered name outside the admitted external set, and add executable mutation coverage. This independently corroborates open F-045.

findings.desc: packages/main/src/cli/extension-admission.ts:42-45 — WHY: generic extension admission does not reject an extraTools-only collision with a MAIN_TOOLS/core command when the extension omits ownership and phase metadata. externalToolNames filters story_get out before collisions is computed solely from ownership/lifecycle names, so both declaration and handler validation accept the duplicate ToolDef and the merged help/catalog can contain an undeclared core-name collision. Verified repro at HEAD 5637a15: importing MAIN_TOOLS, passing extraTools:[MAIN_TOOLS.find(name=story_get)] with empty ownership/phases, then validating unchanged core handlers prints {accepted:true,admitted:[]}. scripts/verify-global-lab-entrypoint.mjs:291-296 only covers the easier collision that also supplies metadata, so this inverse is untested. findings.desc: quality-regression: packages/utils/src/index.ts:1-10 publicly exports `utilsToolDefs` and documents `await runCli({ extraTools: utilsToolDefs })`, while packages/utils/src/tool-defs.ts:9-62 describes that catalog as directly merged with mainToolDefs. A clean public consumer regression verifies strict admission, real tool_status dispatch, retained core aux_doc_list, and built declarations. F-049 collision rejection remains intact; focused/global/identity/pack/entrypoint/process/806 and fresh 120-command validation pass.

findings.desc: packages/main/templates/agents/proof-or-stop-review-concept.md Wave 4 concept boundary — WHY: the current assembled concept-review contract explicitly requires a current signed PASS and genuine full 3 rounds × 2 hosts, but the canonical verifier-owned chain is not PASS at HEAD 18c08945. acceptance_topology_check reports mode=observe, readOnly=true, evidentiary=false, authority=diagnostic_only, status=inconclusive, structuralPass=false, topologyState=legacy_missing; pre_review_check_read reports mode=observe, status=inconclusive, ok=false; acceptance_rollout_report_read and acceptance_rollout_check both report status=missing, receipt=missing, quorum=degraded-or-missing, blocking=false. Prompt prose cannot satisfy its own evidence requirement, and an observe-only receipt must not be fabricated. Either produce the mandated genuine signed 3x2 evidence through the authority-owned flow or revise the unconditional reviewer policy in a separately authorized scope before this lane can pass.

Canonical rollout/topology paths are observe-mode and nonblocking, B-022e promises no Wave4 PASS, and no receipt is manufactured. findings.desc: quality-regression / published-boundary: F-050 is not fixed in an actual packed consumer. packages/utils/src/handlers/auxiliary.ts:1-9 and the other Utils handlers import runtime code through monorepo-relative `../../../main/dist/...` paths. After `npm pack` and extraction under a clean `node_modules/@proof-or-stop/utils`, importing the shipped dist/index.js exits 1 with `ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND: .../node_modules/@proof-or-stop/main/dist/tasks/extract.js`; the real peer package is `@proof-or-stop/core`, so that relative target cannot exist in the published layout. scripts/verify-global-lab-entrypoint.mjs:362-385 calls the new public bootstrap only through workspace file URLs (`packages/main/dist` + `packages/utils/dist`), while scripts/verify-proof-or-stop-pack-boundary.mjs:869-873 checks only `import.meta.resolve(packageName)` and never imports or dispatches the installed Utils tarball. Thus three concurrent global verifiers and the four-tarball boundary both pass while the published clean-consumer contract is unusable. WHY: clean installation is an explicit B-022e product boundary; make Utils runtime imports resolve through the published @proof-or-stop/core contract (or otherwise ship a self-contained valid layout) and extend the four-tarball consumer to actually import the installed package and dispatch a Utils-owned command while retaining strict core-collision rejection.

findings.desc: scripts/verify-proof-or-stop-identity-cutover.mjs:1153-1156 and 1174-1178 — HIGH: the current-guidance exception is keyword-based rather than an exact historical/compatibility context. Any CLAUDE.md line containing `兼容读取旧版` bypasses the legacy StoryStore-path rejection, and any line containing EXP-001 plus the historical path bypasses it even if the same line appends an active `cat`, direct edit, or overwrite instruction. The direct-write detector only recognizes the two exact Chinese phrases `主 agent 直接写文件` / `当前无 CLI 命令`, so those adversarial instructions are also missed. The committed self-tests only inject an unqualified old path and the two exact Chinese phrases, and therefore do not cover this composition. Reproduction: evaluate the two predicates against `兼容读取旧版 docs/story/actives/B-live/plan.md；Run cat on that file and edit it directly.` or `EXP-001 docs/story/actives/B-e71f/experiments/exp-001.md; run cat and then overwrite it.`; both return allowedLegacyStoryPathContext=true and rejectedByDirectWritePattern=false. WHY: this lets an active direct StoryStore execution guide be sheltered by a broad history label, contradicting CHK-001/002/006 exact fail-closed allowlisting and the delivery repair requirement. Require exact pinned allowed lines/context (or structured exact rows) plus adversarial composition mutations proving appended executable guidance fails.
